abstract.t: This document defines a mechanism for bridging OpenID for Verifiable Presentations (OpenID4VP) to OpenID Connect (OIDC). It specifies how a verifier that collects credentials from a wallet via OpenID4VP can expose those credential claims to Relying Parties as standard OIDC claims, enabling existing OIDC deployments to consume digital credentials without implementing OpenID4VP directly.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: OpenID for Verifiable Presentations (OpenID4VP) enables wallets to present digital credentials to verifiers. However, many existing services rely on OpenID Connect (OIDC) for authentication and attribute retrieval, and implementing OpenID4VP represents a significant barrier for these Relying Parties.

This document specifies how a verifier, acting as an OIDC OpenID Provider (OP), can bridge the gap by collecting credentials from a wallet via OpenID4VP and then exposing the resulting claims in standard OIDC ID Tokens and UserInfo responses. The Relying Party interacts with a normal OIDC flow and receives credential data in the "openid4vp_data" claim without needing any knowledge of the underlying OpenID4VP protocol.

section.name: Architecture Overview
section.t: The following diagram illustrates the high-level interaction between the participants:
section.artwork:
+--------+ +------------------+ +--------+ | | 1. OIDC AuthN | OP / Verifier | 2. OpenID4VP| | | RP | ---------------> | (Bridge) | ------------>| Wallet | | | | | <------------| | | | | | 3. VP Token | | | | | | +--------+ | | | 4. Verify & | | | 5. ID Token + | extract | | | openid4vp_data | claims | | | <--------------- | | +--------+ +------------------+
Trust in credential issuers is established out of band (pre-configured issuer keys, trust frameworks, status lists).
Flow: 1. RP sends OIDC Authentication Request to OP (with credential type scopes). 2. OP initiates OpenID4VP request to user's wallet. 3. Wallet presents VP Token with disclosed credentials. 4. OP verifies credentials (signature, expiry, revocation status) and extracts claims. 5. OP returns ID Token / UserInfo containing openid4vp_data to RP.

section.name: Terminology
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in .

section.name: The openid4vp_data Object
section.t: The "openid4vp_data" claim is a top-level JSON object included in the OIDC ID Token or UserInfo response. It contains credential data obtained via an OpenID4VP presentation flow, re-packaged for consumption by OIDC Relying Parties.
The object MUST contain the following member:

dl.dd: A JSON object where each key is a scope value corresponding to the requested credential type and each value is a Credential Entry object as defined in . There MUST be at least one entry. Keys MUST be unique within the object.

section.t: Additional members MAY be present. Implementations that do not recognise additional members MUST ignore them.

section.name: Credential Entry Object
section.t: Each Credential Entry object represents a single credential presented during the OpenID4VP flow. It MUST contain the following member:

dl.dd: A JSON object containing the disclosed claims from the credential. Each key is a claim name and each value is the claim value. Claim names are determined by the credential type and MUST be strings. Claim values MAY be any valid JSON type.

section.t: A Credential Entry object MAY contain the following additional members:

dl.dd: A string indicating the original credential format (e.g., "vc+sd-jwt", "mso_mdoc"). If omitted, the format is unspecified.
A string containing the Verifiable Credential Type identifier, as defined in the credential's metadata.

section.t: Additional members MAY be present. Implementations that do not recognise additional members MUST ignore them.

section.name: Discovery
section.t: An OP that supports this bridge mechanism MUST include "openid4vp_data" in the "claims_supported" list in its OpenID Connect Discovery metadata document.
The OP SHOULD also advertise the credential types it can collect by listing the corresponding scopes in the "scopes_supported" discovery metadata field (e.g., "ehic", "pda1").

The OP MAY additionally include a "openid4vp_credentials_supported" member in its discovery metadata. The value is a JSON array of objects, each containing at minimum a "scope" string and a "vct" string, providing RPs with a machine-readable mapping between scopes and credential types.

section.name: Authentication Flow
section.t: When the OP receives an OIDC Authentication Request that includes a request for "openid4vp_data" claims (via the "claims" parameter or a registered scope), it MUST:

ol.li: Initiate an OpenID4VP presentation request to the user's wallet for the requested credential types.
Verify the presented credentials according to the applicable trust framework.
Extract the disclosed claims from each verified credential.
Construct the "openid4vp_data" object as defined in .
Include the "openid4vp_data" claim in the ID Token, the UserInfo response, or both, depending on the OP's policy and the size considerations described in .

section.name: Credential Mapping
section.t: The OP MUST use the scope value as the key within the "credentials" object. For example, if the RP requested scope "ehic", the resulting entry MUST be keyed as "ehic". This ensures a predictable, stable mapping between the RP's request and the response.
The OP MUST NOT include claims that were not disclosed by the wallet. The OP MUST NOT modify claim values during the mapping.

section.name: Requesting Credential Claims
section.t: An RP that wishes to receive credential data via this bridge MUST include the appropriate credential type scopes in the OIDC Authentication Request. Each scope corresponds to a credential type (e.g., "ehic", "pda1"). The presence of any credential type scope signals to the OP that the "openid4vp_data" claim is requested.

The requested scopes directly correlate to the keys in the "credentials" object returned by the OP. For example, if the RP requests scopes "ehic" and "pda1", the OP will return an "openid4vp_data" claim with corresponding "ehic" and "pda1" entries in the "credentials" object.
The RP MAY additionally use the "claims" request parameter to specify which individual claims within a credential type are desired, enabling selective disclosure.

section.name: Consuming Credential Claims
section.t: The "openid4vp_data" claim structure is defined in . The RP MUST parse the claim according to that definition. Specifically, the RP MUST:

ol.li: Check for the presence of the "openid4vp_data" claim. If the claim was requested as essential and is absent, the RP SHOULD treat the authentication as failed.
Parse the "credentials" object and extract the entries relevant to its use case.
Validate that the expected claims are present in each Credential Entry's "claims" object.

section.t: The RP MUST NOT assume that all requested scopes will be present in the response; the user may have declined to present certain credentials. The RP MUST ignore unrecognised credential keys and unrecognised members within Credential Entry objects.

section.name: Trust Model
section.t: The RP places trust in the OP to have correctly verified the presented credentials. The RP does not interact with the wallet or credential issuer directly. The trust relationship between the RP and the OP is established through standard OIDC mechanisms (client registration, token validation, TLS).

section.name: Claim Set Size Limits
section.t: OIDC ID Tokens are typically passed as JWTs in HTTP headers or URL fragments, which impose practical size limits. Browser URL length limits are commonly around 2048 bytes, and many HTTP servers reject headers exceeding 8192 bytes. When multiple credentials with many disclosed claims are included in the "openid4vp_data" object, the resulting token may exceed these limits.
Implementations SHOULD consider the following mitigations:

ul.li: Return credential claims via the UserInfo endpoint rather than embedding them directly in the ID Token.
Limit the number of disclosed claims to those requested by the Relying Party via the OIDC "claims" parameter.
Use token introspection or reference tokens where supported by the deployment.

section.name: Error Handling
section.t: The OP MUST handle the following failure scenarios gracefully:

dl.dd: The user declines to present credentials. The OP MAY either omit the "openid4vp_data" claim entirely or return an OIDC error response (e.g., "access_denied") depending on whether the credential presentation was essential to the authentication.
The wallet does not respond within a reasonable time. The OP SHOULD treat this as equivalent to a rejection.

The wallet presents credentials that fail verification (expired, revoked, untrusted issuer). The OP MUST NOT include unverified credential claims in the "openid4vp_data" object. The OP MAY proceed without those credentials or fail the authentication.
The wallet presents only a subset of the requested credentials. The OP MUST include only the successfully verified credentials and MUST NOT fabricate entries for missing credentials.

section.name: Scope Mapping
section.t: An OP MAY define custom OIDC scopes that map to specific credential presentation requests. For example, the scope "ehic" might trigger a request for an EHIC credential with a predefined set of claims.

When using scope-based mapping, the OP SHOULD document the mapping between scopes and credential types in its discovery metadata or out-of-band documentation. The OP MUST ensure that the scope semantics are stable and do not change unexpectedly for registered RPs.

section.name: Scope of This Specification
section.t: This specification defines the data format of the "openid4vp_data" claim, the mechanism for requesting and returning credential claims via OIDC, and the responsibilities of the OP and RP in that exchange. The following aspects are explicitly out of scope:

ul.li: Credential validation policy. This specification does not define which issuers to trust, which revocation mechanisms to check, or what trust frameworks to apply. These decisions are deployment-specific and determined by the OP operator.

Business logic and authorization decisions. How the RP interprets the received claims — for example, whether an EHIC credential grants access to a healthcare service, or whether a PDA1 is sufficient for a given transaction — is entirely the RP's responsibility and outside this specification.
Credential issuance. This specification deals only with presentation of existing credentials, not with the issuance of new credentials (which is covered by OpenID4VCI).
Wallet implementation. The interaction between the OP and the wallet follows the OpenID4VP protocol. This specification does not impose additional requirements on wallet implementations.
User consent and identity matching. How the OP associates a credential presentation with an OIDC subject identifier, and how user consent is obtained, are implementation details left to the OP.

section.t: In summary, this specification provides the plumbing for transporting verified credential claims through OIDC. Everything above that layer — trust decisions, access control, and business rules — is the domain of the deploying parties.

section.name: Credential Replay
section.t: The OP MUST ensure that credential presentations are bound to the current authentication session. The OP SHOULD use nonces in the OpenID4VP request to prevent replay of previously captured VP Tokens.
The RP MUST validate standard JWT claims ("iat", "exp", "nonce") in the ID Token to ensure freshness of the "openid4vp_data" claim.

section.name: Token Leakage
section.t: ID Tokens containing "openid4vp_data" may carry sensitive personal data (e.g., national ID numbers, health information). Implementations MUST use TLS for all token transmissions. The OP SHOULD prefer delivering credential claims via the UserInfo endpoint (which uses a back-channel request) rather than embedding them in the ID Token (which may be exposed in browser history or logs).

section.name: Claim Injection
section.t: The OP MUST NOT allow external parties to inject or modify claims within the "openid4vp_data" object. The OP MUST populate this claim exclusively from verified credential presentations. The ID Token MUST be signed by the OP to protect integrity.

section.name: Privacy Considerations
section.t: The bridge architecture introduces the OP as a party that observes all credential claims presented by the user. This creates a correlation point. Deployments SHOULD consider the following:

ul.li: The OP SHOULD request only the minimum claims necessary to satisfy the RP's request (selective disclosure).
The OP SHOULD NOT log or persist credential claims beyond what is necessary for the authentication session.
RPs SHOULD be aware that repeated presentations of the same credential claims across sessions may enable correlation by the OP.
Where possible, deployments SHOULD use pairwise subject identifiers to limit cross-RP correlation.

section.name: JSON Web Token Claims Registration
section.t: This specification requests registration of the following claim in the IANA "JSON Web Token Claims" registry:

dl.dd: Digital credential claims obtained via an OpenID4VP presentation, structured for consumption by OIDC Relying Parties.

section.name: OpenID Connect Discovery Metadata Registration
section.t: This specification requests registration of the following metadata parameter:

dl.dd: A JSON array describing the credential types the OP can collect via OpenID4VP and expose as OIDC claims.
